A specialized training program to improve phonologic awareness as a basis for reading and writing in every kindergarten and preschool child seems to be unnecessary, according to the retrieved matches. However, children with temporary hearing deficits benefit from such a program. For all other children, general perception training may be sufficient.

In summary, while specialized training of phonological awareness is not required for every preschool child, it can be beneficial for some children with temporary hearing deficits, and general perception training may suffice for the majority of children.
